scenes.text: What $15 a day turns into if you invest it for 20 years

script.caption:
$15 a day is $450 a month. Here's what that becomes in an index fund if it averages 8% a year:

After 10 years: you put in $54,000, it's worth about $82,000
After 20 years: you put in $108,000, it's worth about $265,000

More than half of that 20-year number is growth, not money you put in. That's compounding.

Where the $15 comes from: one takeout meal or two café drinks a day.

A few things that matter:
1. Use your TFSA so the growth isn't taxed
2. Turn on dividend reinvestment (DRIP)
3. Don't sell when the market drops

8% isn't guaranteed. Some years are down. But over 20 years, starting matters more than picking the perfect fund.

scenes.text: The true cost of paying the minimum on credit cards

script.caption:
Credit card companies love the minimum payment. Here's why.

Say you have $3,000 on a regular 20.99% card and you pay 3% a month, which is a common minimum. It takes almost 19 years to pay off, and you pay about $3,900 in interest. More than you spent.

How to get out faster:

1. Pay more than the minimum (Saved: ~$200/mo in interest)
Even an extra $50 a month cuts years off.

2. Go after the highest rate first (Saved: ~$150/mo)
Minimum on everything, every extra dollar on the card with the highest interest.

3. Take your card off your phone and online stores (Saved: ~$100/mo)
It's hard to pay down a card you keep using.

4. Keep $1,000 in cash (Saved: ~$100/mo)
So the next surprise bill doesn't go right back on the card.

Your statement shows how long the minimum would take. Look at it once.

scenes.text: What $200 a month in the S&P 500 could turn into if you never sell

script.caption:
You don't need to pick stocks or watch charts all day.

$200 a month into an S&P 500 index fund for 20 years, if it averages 8% a year: you put in $48,000, and it's worth about $118,000.

What actually matters:
1. Keep buying every month, good market or bad (Saved: ~$200/mo)
2. Don't sell during dips. The S&P 500 has recovered from every crash so far, including 2008 and 2020
3. Turn on dividend reinvestment (Saved: ~$50/mo)
4. Delete the trading app if it makes you want to day trade

Not guaranteed, and past returns don't promise future ones. But boring and consistent usually wins.
